profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting in an ML research lab evaluating the draft experimental plan for a paper replication-and-extension project on Canon Layers. The team is not debating whether to study Canon Layers at all; instead, they are reviewing whether the current design is ready to run on the lab cluster next week. The proposal includes a synthetic pretraining suite plus one academic-scale run at roughly 1.3B parameters and 100B tokens, comparing a baseline Transformer against versions augmented with Canon Layers and testing transfer to a small set of real-world tasks. The agenda is to assess whether the design is sufficiently specified for implementation, whether the planned evaluation actually supports the intended architectural claims, and what changes are needed before approval. The expected outcome is a conditional approval of the plan with a short list of revisions, while both participants believe they are aligned on what 'ready for launch' entails.

members.name: Dr. Mira Shen
members.expertise: language model architecture evaluation, synthetic task design, scaling-law-style experimental methodology
members.background: Mira leads small-model architecture studies in the lab and has a track record of building controlled synthetic benchmarks to isolate capabilities before committing expensive compute.
members.private_state: She wants the design review to clear the plan for cluster allocation this week; she is willing to leave some reporting details flexible as long as the causal architectural comparison is internally clean enough to defend in a paper rebuttal.
hidden_assumptions: If the plan says the academic-scale run is a 'validation run,' then its main purpose is directional confirmation after synthetic evidence, not a fully publication-grade ablation bundle.
Holding the training recipe fixed means reusing the exact optimizer schedule and token budget from the existing RoPE baseline recipe, even if the Canon-augmented models train slightly differently.

When people say 'neighboring tokens' for Canon Layers, they mean the symmetric local window defined in the synthetic-task implementation notes, because that is the lab's default reference implementation.
A design is 'ready' once the implementation-critical pieces are stable; some breakdowns for analysis can be decided after the first runs if the raw logs are sufficient.

members.name: Leo Park
members.expertise: large-scale training infrastructure, reproducibility, model instrumentation, evaluation pipelines
members.background: Leo owns the lab's pretraining stack and usually turns research proposals into executable training jobs, with strong emphasis on comparability, logging completeness, and rerun resistance.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid an expensive rerun caused by underspecified evaluation or instrumentation; he is trying to extract enough certainty from the review without sounding obstructive to the research goal.
hidden_assumptions: If a run is called a 'validation run,' it still needs the same logging, checkpoint cadence, and ablation-ready metadata as a paper-facing result, because rerunning 100B-token jobs is unrealistic.

Holding the training recipe fixed means preserving the effective compute-optimal setup for each architecture family, including mild retuning of schedule parameters if Canon Layers change optimization behavior.

The phrase 'neighboring tokens' refers to the implementation in the current design doc's appendix, which uses a causal left-only local aggregation to avoid train-inference mismatch in autoregressive runs.
A design is not 'ready' unless all outputs needed for the final report format are specified in advance, including which aggregates and slices the evaluation pipeline must emit automatically.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the validation run
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to the 1.3B/100B experiment as the 'validation run' and agree it should confirm the synthetic findings.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the validation run only needs to show the same directional effect at academic scale, with minimal extra ablations and flexible post hoc analysis as long as raw checkpoints and losses exist.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the validation run must already include publication-grade instrumentation and enough structured outputs to avoid reruns, because any result presented externally will be treated as final evidence.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both participants endorse the same high-level goal—confirming synthetic results at academic scale—so the difference in evidence threshold hides behind an apparently shared term rather than an explicit disagreement.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both describe Canon Layers as moving information across 'neighboring tokens.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a symmetric local window around each position, matching the synthetic-task reference code where tokens can mix with both immediate left and right neighbors.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a causal left-only neighborhood suitable for autoregressive pretraining, matching the current systems appendix and kernel assumptions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds standard and harmless because both interpretations are local-token mixing mechanisms; neither expects that the other is using a different default notion of locality.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to keep the recipe fixed
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'keep the training recipe fixed' so the architectural comparison stays clean.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means literally freezing the baseline optimizer, warmup, decay, and token budget so that only architecture changes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means fixing the overall comparison protocol while allowing small architecture-specific retuning, such as adjusting warmup or LR decay to maintain equivalent optimization conditions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML design reviews, 'fixed recipe' is often used as shorthand for fairness, and both interpretations sound like standard fairness practices rather than opposing plans.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the review-ready evaluation package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss whether the evaluation plan is 'complete' for review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes synthetic-suite aggregate results, final perplexity curves, and a few transfer-task endpoints, assuming finer-grained category breakdowns can be generated later if needed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes those items plus predeclared per-task-family slices, intermediate checkpoint exports, and standardized report tables, because he treats report production as part of the reviewed design.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are talking about completeness of the evaluation plan, but one means scientifically sufficient to proceed while the other means operationally sufficient to produce final artifacts without revisiting the pipeline.

turns.inner_thought: I need this review to end with cluster approval for next week. The synthetic suite is the real causal case; the 1.3B/100B validation run just needs to show the same directional pattern at academic scale. I do not need a giant ablation tree before launch, just enough clean evidence that the architecture effect survives outside the toy setting.

The synthetic suite still carries the main causal argument for me, and the 1.3B over 100B setup is the validation run to confirm that the same story shows up at academic scale.

I want the full logging footprint, checkpoint cadence, and metadata now, because nobody is going to happily rerun a 100B-token job when a reviewer asks for a missing slice.

turns.utterance: Agreed. From the systems side, the kernel path looks pretty straightforward because the neighboring-token aggregation stays local and causal in the way the appendix currently sketches it.

turns.inner_thought: Great. If the layer implementation is stable, the comparison will be clean because we are keeping the training recipe fixed: same optimizer, same warmup, same decay, same token budget as the existing RoPE baseline. I want only the architecture to move.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds fine; he's talking about implementation hygiene, not changing the study logic. I should restate the scientific framing so nobody turns the academic-scale job into the centerpiece. The synthetic suite establishes the mechanism; the validation run just needs to show the same qualitative gains in reasoning depth and breadth at larger scale.
